article_context: Body image illustrating the immersive Jurassic-world flight attraction “На крыльях ветра,” supporting the article’s promise of one-ticket access to vivid, adventurous experiences and introducing the recommended park routes.
image_reading: A dark, rigid foreground ride structure contains multiple suspended seats and visible rider silhouettes facing a large projected prehistoric landscape.
One projected pterosaur is already airborne near the upper-right area of the screen, with wings extended and a rider-like figure visible on its back.

The projected pterosaur’s wing articulation supports limited airborne motion, but its exact flight direction is ambiguous; the seats, rails, supports, silhouettes, and screen boundary provide no evidence of safe mechanical movement.

models.positive_prompt: The projected pterosaur makes one slow, shallow wingbeat in place, then drifts slightly inward while remaining fully inside the existing screen and clear of the upper-right crop. Keep the camera fixed and all foreground seats, riders, rails, supports, attachment points, and the screen boundary rigid; it ends airborne with wings extended, with no added ride rows or objects.
models.scene_plan: Across four seconds, the projected pterosaur begins from its existing wings-extended airborne pose, performs one restrained down-and-up wingbeat at an even pace, and shifts only slightly inward from the upper-right edge. The camera remains fixed with zero screen travel. Near the end, the wings settle into an extended glide pose while the pterosaur stays continuously visible; every foreground seat, rider silhouette, rail, support, attachment point, and the existing projected-screen boundary remains rigid and unchanged, and no new structure or scenery is introduced.
